newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Lower Lauritzen 1996 losses seen.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Lower Lauritzen 1996 losses seen.

text.p: Danish shipping and shipbuilding group J.Lauritzen Holding said on Thursday it expected greatly reduced whole year 1996 losses for its shipping operations, with a small profit seen in 1997.
"We will have a negative net result for full year 1996, but I still expect that it will be near zero," J.Lauritzen A/S managing director Claus V. Ipsen told Reuters in an interview.
"We anticipate a swing back into profit for shipping operations in 1997," he added.
J.Lauritzen, the shipping unit under J.Lauritzen Holding A/S, posted a 115 million crown net loss for full year 1995.

The holding company, hit by the weaker dollar, tough competition and major losses in shipbuilding operations, had a 900 million crown net loss after minorities in 1995 and has forecast a 300 million crown group loss for 1996.

Ipsen attributed the brighter prospects for the shipping unit to a better than expected performance by Lauritzen Reefers' refrigerated cargo division while dry cargo and gas tanker divisions Lauritzen Bulkers and Lauritzen Kosan Tankers did less well last year.
Prospects for Lauritzen Reefers and Lauritzen Kosan Tankers looked brighter though for 1997, he said.
"1997 will see increases in freighting rates of between 10-15 percent but rising oil prices are a problem. Oil is a good deal more expensive than we expected five to six months ago," Ipsen said.
He said Lauritzen Kosan Tankers were expected to benefit from the economic upturn in Europe this year, after being hit by higher gas prices and dwindling demand in 1996.
Ipsen added that the adoption of new accounting methods would improve the full year 1996 J. Lauritzen shipping result by some 30 million crowns.
"But we would have posted a near-balanced result for 1996 regardless of whether we used the new or the old accounting system," Ipsen said.
J.Lauritzen Holding A/S is to unveil its full year 1996 result in March.
